title: model loading breadcrumbs - weights sharding failure (scratchpad)
short_summary: Scratchpad tracing a repeated failure when loading sharded weights from S3 for a customer model. Notes commands tried, error snippets, quick hypotheses and next steps.
content:
Context:
- Repro on dev box (g4dn.xlarge) and on dedicated pool node (same kernel + CUDA). Model: customer-custom-rw-1 (based on rw-medium-v2 checkpoint). Checkpoint is sharded into 8 .pt shards plus metadata/index.json produced by our export script.
- Failure observed during weights download + mmap / load stage (the process exits with non-zero). Happens ~30-40% of the time for a given node; rest of runs succeed.
- Suspect either intermittent S3 network errors + partial writes, or race in our shard-reassembly / mmap logic when concurrent readers racing on same tmp file.

Repro steps (what I run locally):
1) Clean workspace
   rm -rf /tmp/ckpt-test && mkdir -p /tmp/ckpt-test
2) Download shards (simulate runtime flow)
   aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/customer-custom-rw-1/index.json /tmp/ckpt-test/index.json
   for i in `seq 0 7`; do aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/customer-custom-rw-1/shard_$i.pt /tmp/ckpt-test/; done
3) Run runner
   python -m rwinference.runner --model-dir /tmp/ckpt-test --device cuda:0 --log-level debug

Commands tried (to narrow down):
- aws s3 cp with and without --no-verify-ssl
- aws s3 cp with --request-payer (not applicable) — no change
- gsutil rsync (N/A: s3) — tried rclone copy s3:bucket/ckpt /tmp -> same failures
- curl from presigned URLs for individual shards -> reproduces failure sometimes
- md5/sha256 checks on downloaded shards -> sometimes mismatch; other times OK
- stat and open in python to test partial file detection (os.path.getsize differs from expected size)
- tried writing to unique temp filenames and rename into place (atomically) to test race hypothesis

Observed errors (raw snippets):
- During download: "ConnectionResetError: [Errno 104] Connection reset by peer" from botocore
- During load: "RuntimeError: expected tensor with 2 dimensions but got 0" (likely truncated shard) — stack shows torch.load failing midway
- mmap/perm issues: "OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument" on os.mmap when mapping file created by concurrent writer
- Integrity errors: "sha256 mismatch for shard_3.pt (expected a1b2..., got 0000...)"
- Occasionally: "Killed" (OOM) right after torch.load starts — but mem usage < instance total; probably fragmentation from multiple processes

Hypotheses:
1) Network/transient download corruption
   - Evidence: connection resets + occasional checksum mismatches
   - Counter: same S3 object sometimes downloads correctly multiple times
2) Concurrent writer/reader race in our download+load pipeline
   - Evidence: mapping errors and invalid argument when mmap invoked; rename-into-place reduced failures locally
   - Counter: failures still occur even when we write to unique tmp files then os.rename
3) Checkpoint format mismatch (export used float16 quantization but loader expects float32)
   - Evidence: type errors seen in some stack traces when dtype mismatch
   - Counter: index.json reports dtype float16; loader should handle that path
4) Partial retry logic in transfer layer leaves 0-byte or truncated files if interrupted
   - Evidence: truncated sizes and zero-hash occurrences
5) Filesystem-level caching / NFS weirdness on dedicated pool (but repro on local ephemeral SSD too)

Notes from experiments:
- Writing to unique filenames + fsync + atomic rename into final path dropped repro rate from ~35% to ~5% on my laptop. That points strongly to race or partial-write visibility.
- Adding an explicit checksum verification (sha256) after download and redownload-on-mismatch fixes 100% of cases in loopback tests. But needs to be upstreamed (extra S3 egress + latency cost).
- Using boto3 s3transfer with "use_threads=False" reduced connection reset frequency (maybe thread pool overloading sockets). Worth testing further.
- When the loader does mmap on a file that is still being written, Linux can succeed but content may be partial/truncated leading to torch.load failing with cryptic errors.

Quick patches tried (local):
- pipeline change: download -> write to /tmp/ckpt-$$/shard_i.pt.tmp -> fsync -> os.rename into /tmp/ckpt/shard_i.pt
- add explicit sha256 check against index.json (index had precomputed checksums)
- retry logic: up to 3 attempts per shard with exponential backoff
- make boto3 s3 client use max_concurrency=4
Result: on dev machine, these reduced failure to near 0 for 200 runs.

Edge cases observed:
- index.json sometimes missing checksums (older exports); we need to fall back to size-based sanity checks there
- Some customers store checkpoints behind CloudFront with short presigned lifetime -> presigned link expiry can cause mid-download resets
- When multiple downloads run in parallel on same node (batching), socket exhaustion + ephemeral port reuse increases connection resets. Limiting concurrency helps.

Next steps / action items:
- Short term (patch in week):
  - Add atomic-write + fsync + rename for shard downloads in loader (low-risk).
  - Add optional checksum verification step using index.json (configurable via env var to avoid 2x cost always).
  - Reduce default s3 transfer concurrency on smaller instance types.
- Medium term:
  - Add server-side support for range-based retryable downloads (so incomplete ranges can be retried instead of full re-download).
  - Add CI test that simulates partial-file visibility (writer sleeps before rename) to catch race regressions.
  - Investigate whether we can reuse presigned URLs differently for long-running downloads (refresh token) for behind-CF setups.
- Observability:
  - Add metrics: shard_download_failures, shard_checksum_mismatch, shard_rename_failures, shard_concurrency_throttle
  - Log full checksum + size on success for forensic replay

Questions for Jordan / SRE:
- Do we have known issues with our dedicated pool nodes using NFS or other shared mounts that could cause atomic rename semantics to differ? (I saw both ephemeral SSD and dedicated pool repro so likely not only NFS)
- Any infra-level rate limits we should be aware of between our nodes and S3 (burstable connections per IP)?

Raw commands / snippets kept here for quick copy:
- download loop
for i in `seq 0 7`; do 
  aws s3 cp s3://redwood-checkpoints/customer-custom-rw-1/shard_$i.pt /tmp/ckpt-test/shard_$i.pt.tmp && \n  sync && \n  mv /tmp/ckpt-test/shard_$i.pt.tmp /tmp/ckpt-test/shard_$i.pt || echo "DL_FAIL $i"
  done

- sha256 check
expected=$(jq -r ".shards[$i].sha256" index.json)
actual=$(sha256sum shard_$i.pt | awk '{print $1}')
if [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then echo "MISMATCH $i"; fi

- python snippet used to simulate mmap race
with open(shard_path, 'rb') as f:
    mm = mmap.mmap(f.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
    # parse header bytes
    magic = mm.read(8)
    if magic != b'TCKPTv1\x00':
        raise RuntimeError('invalid header')

- earlier stack excerpt (trimmed):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 555, in load
    return _legacy_load(opened_file, map_location, pickle_module)
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/serialization.py", line 803, in _legacy_load
    deserialized_storage_keys, all_storage_shapes = _validate_and_build_tensor_type_map(
RuntimeError: storage size mismatch for key "model.layers.6.weight"

Notes-to-self:
- Push atomic-write + checksum patch to a feature branch and run nightly stress on dedicated pool for 48h.
- If checksum not present in index.json, compute expected sha256 for each shard at export time and include it (ask model-export infra team).
- Consider making checksum verification opt-in with env REDWOOD_CHECKPOINT_VERIFY=1 to avoid cold-start latency on large models.

End of scratchpad. Will iterate once I get Jordan's feedback on infra limits and SRE perspective.
